symptom: PC on VLAN 30 cannot reach anything, including its own gateway.
expected_fault: Switchport assigned to default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30
ai_root_cause: Switchport Gi0/3 is assigned to VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30, preventing the PC from accessing its intended network
ai_evidence: show interfaces Gi0/3 switchport shows Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default) rather than VLAN 30

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN cannot ping each other despite correct IP addresses.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 not included in the allowed VLAN list on the trunk
ai_root_cause: VLAN 20 is not allowed on the trunk between the two switches, so PCs on VLAN 20 cannot forward frames
ai_evidence: show interfaces trunk shows Allowed VLANs: 1,10,40, missing VLAN 20

symptom: New VLAN created but devices assigned to it still can't communicate; VLAN not visible on other switch.
expected_fault: VLAN not propagated due to VTP mode mismatch (Switch A in transparent mode)
ai_root_cause: VTP configuration on Switch B is preventing VLAN 60 from propagating
ai_evidence: show vlan brief Switch B shows VLAN 60 not listed

symptom: Voice VLAN phone fails to register; data still passes fine from the same port.
expected_fault: Voice VLAN not configured on the switchport
ai_root_cause: Voice VLAN not configured on Gi0/7, so the IP phone cannot register
ai_evidence: show interfaces Gi0/7 switchport shows Voice VLAN: none

symptom: PC can ping its own IP and other PCs on the same subnet, but not the default gateway.
expected_fault: VLAN 10 SVI is administratively down
ai_root_cause: VLAN10 SVI is administratively down, so the gateway 192.168.10.1 is unreachable
ai_evidence: show ip interface brief shows Vlan10 administratively down

symptom: PC cannot reach gateway even though gateway interface shows up/up.
expected_fault: Incorrect default gateway configured on the PC (mismatched with actual SVI IP)
ai_root_cause: PC configured with incorrect default gateway

symptom: Intermittent gateway reachability; ping succeeds sometimes and times out other times.
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address on the network causing ARP conflict
ai_root_cause: Duplicate IP address 192.168.30.1 causing ARP conflicts
ai_evidence: show ip arp shows two MACs for same IP

symptom: All PCs on a subnet lose gateway access after a switch reboot.
expected_fault: SVI line protocol down, likely no active ports assigned to VLAN 40 after reboot
ai_root_cause: VLAN 40 SVI is administratively down after reboot
ai_evidence: show ip interface brief shows Vlan40 down down

symptom: New PC gets a 169.254.x.x address instead of an IP from the DHCP server.
expected_fault: Missing ip helper-address on VLAN 30 SVI, so DHCP requests never reach the server
ai_root_cause: Missing IP helper-address on VLAN 30

symptom: Some PCs on a VLAN get IP addresses, others do not.
expected_fault: DHCP pool exhausted, no addresses left to lease
ai_root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN20 is exhausted

symptom: PC receives an IP address from the wrong subnet.
expected_fault: DHCP pool for VLAN10 mistakenly configured with VLAN20's subnet
ai_root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN10 configured with wrong subnet

symptom: PC fails to renew IP lease and drops off the network periodically.
expected_fault: DHCP lease time set too short, causing frequent renewal failures under load
ai_root_cause: DHCP lease time set to 2 minutes causing frequent renewals

symptom: PC can ping a server by IP but cannot reach it by hostname.
expected_fault: Incorrect or unreachable DNS server configured on the client
ai_root_cause: DNS server 192.168.100.200 is unreachable

symptom: Internal hostname resolves to the wrong IP address.
expected_fault: Stale DNS A record not updated after server IP change
ai_root_cause: Stale DNS A record for fileserver01

symptom: All external websites fail to load by name, but internal name resolution works.
expected_fault: No external DNS forwarder configured; internal DNS server cannot resolve external names
ai_root_cause: Router lacks external DNS forwarder

symptom: PC can reach its own VLAN's gateway but cannot reach a server in another VLAN.
expected_fault: Missing route or disabled routing between VLAN 30 and VLAN 10
ai_root_cause: Missing inter-VLAN route to 192.168.10.0/24
ai_evidence: show ip route shows no route

symptom: Branch office cannot reach headquarters network over a WAN link.
expected_fault: Missing static route to the remote network on the branch router
ai_root_cause: Missing static route to headquarters network

symptom: Route to a destination exists but traffic is not using it; packets seem to take a longer path.
expected_fault: Incorrect administrative distance or misconfigured routing protocol causing suboptimal path selection
ai_root_cause: EIGRP route not active so falls back to RIP
reviewer_notes: AI misdiagnosed the mechanism — attributed it to EIGRP being inactive rather than incorrect administrative distance. Symptom noticed correctly, root cause wrong.

symptom: OSPF neighbors never form; routes from the neighboring router are missing.
expected_fault: OSPF neighbor adjacency failing due to Hello/Dead timer mismatch between routers
ai_root_cause: OSPF process ID and hello interval mismatch
ai_evidence: Process ID mismatch Hello interval mismatch

symptom: Server that should be reachable from one VLAN is blocked entirely, even for permitted traffic.
expected_fault: ACL rule order is wrong; deny-all placed before the intended permit statement
ai_root_cause: ACL FINANCE-ACL has deny all before permit
ai_evidence: deny ip any any precedes permit

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi devices can reach an internal server that should be isolated.
expected_fault: ACL exists but was never applied to the VLAN 50 interface
ai_root_cause: ACL GUEST-ISOLATION not applied to VLAN 50 SVI
ai_evidence: no access list configured on interface

symptom: Specific host can access a server; the same subnet's other hosts cannot, though they should be able to.
expected_fault: ACL only permits a single host instead of the full subnet as intended
ai_root_cause: ACL permits only host 192.168.30.5

symptom: Remote management access (SSH) to a router stopped working after an ACL update.
expected_fault: ACL on VTY lines references outdated admin IP, blocking current management host
ai_root_cause: ACL MGMT-ACL only permits old admin IP

symptom: Internal PCs cannot reach the internet at all.
expected_fault: NAT inside/outside not applied to the correct interfaces
ai_root_cause: NAT not configured on any interface
reviewer_notes: AI said NAT wasn't configured at all, but expected fault implies it exists just on wrong interfaces — close but not exact.

symptom: Internet works for some internal PCs but not others.
expected_fault: NAT ACL does not include all internal subnets that need translation
ai_root_cause: NAT ACL only permits 192.168.10.0/24

symptom: A specific internal server (should be reachable from the internet) is not accessible externally.
expected_fault: Static NAT entry for the internal server was never configured
ai_root_cause: Static NAT entry for 192.168.10.100 missing

symptom: Laptop cannot see or connect to the office Wi-Fi network at all.
expected_fault: SSID broadcast disabled on the AP, making the network invisible to clients
ai_root_cause: SSID CorpNet broadcast-ssid disabled

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but immediately get disconnected.
expected_fault: Passphrase mismatch between AP and previously saved client profiles causing repeated auth failures
ai_root_cause: Clients authenticating with incorrect WPA2 passphrase
